name: Templo de Debod

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/6432785 (centroid of the outline of the temple; long axis at 77.6°, the entrance faces the gateways to the east)

rights.note: Ancient Egyptian temple (built: AD 14 = end of the last decoration campaign, under Augustus); begun c. 200–180 BC under the Meroitic king Adikhalamani and enlarged under the Ptolemies and Augustus; dismantled in Nubia in 1960–1961, given to Spain in 1968 and rebuilt in Madrid in 1970–1972 by anastylosis (Spanish team directed by Martín Almagro Basch). The pool and terrace are part of the 1972 setting.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1140249_templo_de_debod.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The temple, its annex, the gateways, the terrace and the causeway follow the OpenStreetMap outlines; the pool (not mapped as water in OSM) was measured on the orthophoto. Heights come from photos (±10 %): terrace 1.3 m, temple walls 6.4 m above it with a cavetto cornice on the entrance front, annex ~4.7 m, gateways ~5.5 and ~6.0 m. The pronaos is simplified to four columns with bell-shaped floral capitals, screen walls, a doorway and a winged sun disc; carved reliefs, the interior rooms and the railings are not modelled; the walls are drawn course by course in slightly different sandstone tones. The low grey roof that protects the temple is kept just above the parapet as on the orthophoto. Water is a flat glossy surface 0.2 m below the kerbs. Footprint: the convex hull of the terrace and the pool grown by 1 m (nothing else stands inside).
